title: Lasagne al Forno
subtitle: Classic baked beef lasagne with béchamel
excerpt: The Italian version of baked pasta: slow-cooked beef ragù layered with dried lasagne sheets and a rich béchamel, baked until bubbling and brown-edged. The ragù and béchamel are both made from scratch and the result is nothing like the jarred-sauce version.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lasagne al forno (baked lasagne) as it is understood internationally takes its form from the Emilia-Romagna tradition, where the dish is made with fresh egg pasta, a slow-cooked meat ragù, a proper béchamel, and Parmesan. The version that spread to Britain and to Italian-American cooking in the twentieth century simplified the fresh pasta to dried sheets (which are serviceable and significantly easier) and in some cases replaced the béchamel with ricotta. The original Bologna version uses ragù bolognese as the meat sauce and is one of the great dishes of Italian regional cooking. A proper lasagne is a project: the ragù alone benefits from 2 hours of simmering. Made in advance and refrigerated overnight it improves in flavour and slices more cleanly.

recipeTools.notes: A deep-sided baking dish, about 30 x 20 cm.

content.text: Cook the ragù slowly for a minimum of 1.5 hours; 2 hours is better. It should be thick and almost dry before you layer it: a wet ragù will steam rather than bake the pasta. Lay the dried lasagne sheets in a single layer without overlapping and make sure every sheet is covered in sauce and béchamel on both sides; dry patches will stay hard. The dish benefits from resting for 15 minutes after baking: it slices much more cleanly.

Make the ragù: heat the oil in a large saucepan and cook the onion, carrot, and celery gently for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Increase the heat, add the beef mince and brown, breaking it up. Add the tomato purée, cook for 2 minutes, then add the wine and let it reduce for 3 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, bay, and thyme. Simmer very gently, uncovered, for 90 minutes until thick.

Make the béchamel: melt the butter over medium heat, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Add the warm milk gradually, whisking constantly. Cook, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and smooth. Season with salt and nutmeg.

Heat the oven to 190 C (170 C fan). In a deep baking dish, spread a thin layer of ragù, then a layer of pasta sheets, then ragù, then béchamel. Repeat until the ingredients are used up, finishing with a generous layer of béchamel. Scatter the Parmesan over the top. Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until bubbling and golden-brown. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.
